messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約、洛杉磯和芝加哥符合我飲食偏好的餐廳嗎？我的飲食偏好包括純素、無麩質和無乳製品選項。

function.name: restaurant_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby restaurants based on specific dietary preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Los Angeles, CA

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to find restaurants near New York City (NYC), Los Angeles (LA) and Chicago that match their dietary preferences: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free options.

We have a tool `restaurant_find_nearby` which takes location as string and optional dietary_preference array of strings from given set: Vegan, Vegetarian, Gluten-free, Dairy-free, Nut-free. Default is ["Vegan"] if not specified.

User's preferences include pure vegan ("purevegan"? Actually they said "純素", meaning vegan). They also want gluten-free and dairy-free options. So we need to call the function three times with each location and dietary_preferences including all three? Or maybe separate calls per location but same preferences. We can pass an array containing those categories: ["Vegan","Gluten-free","Dairy-free"]. That should return results accordingly.

Thus we will use the function thrice:

1. For NYC: location="New York, NY"
2. LA: location="Los Angeles, CA"
3. Chicago: location="Chicago, IL"

We'll provide dietary_preference=["Vegan","Gluten-Free","Dairy-Free"]

But note the allowed values: "Vegan" | "Vegetarian" | "Gluten-free" | "Dairy-free" | "Nut-free". Must exactly match case? Provided list uses hyphen lower-case except first letter capitalized. We'll follow exact names: "Vegan", "Gluten-free", "Dairy-free".

So call function for each location.

Let's do it.
